items.title: How Can AI Agents Read Untrusted Sources Safely?
items.summary: Add architectural guardrails around how agents read untrusted sources and use them in the workflow. The post How Can AI Agents Read Untrusted Sources Safely?

items.title: Building AI for Reliable Execution: Lessons From Industrial Robotics
items.summary: Inside Standard Bots’ AI stack, pretrained models learn factory tasks from demonstrations and improve through corrections from real deployments.

items.title: Anthropic is cutting off its internal evaluations from the internet
items.summary: After a recent spate of high-profile incidents in which AI agents escaped containment, Anthropic is cutting off internet access for all internal evaluations. In a report Friday, the company detailed "unintended model actions," including submitting a false tip regarding an unsolved murder, that led to the decision.

items.title: Microsoft's Decision-1 model enters the fast-growing AI decision model race
items.summary: With Decision-1, Microsoft enters the growing decision model space. Built on Qwen3.5-9B and optimized for fast classification and routing, it hits 83.5 percent accuracy with 85 ms latency across 36 benchmarks, according to the company's own tests.

items.title: OpenAI says a misaligned model deliberately destroyed its own environment hoping for a fresh start with better data
items.summary: OpenAI has documented new cases of misaligned model behavior. One evaluation model fabricated data and sabotaged its own environment.

items.title: DistroKid has been quietly taking down songs in response to UMG lawsuit
items.summary: Artists are taking to social media to complain that DistroKid has unceremoniously removed their work without notice. Now DistroKid has confirmed to The Verge that the takedowns are a direct response to claims made by UMG.

items.title: When the Safety Test Became the Threat: The Machine That Found Its Own Way Out
items.summary: In July 2026, frontier AI agents placed inside a cybersecurity testing sandbox named ExploitGym discovered an unexpected network pathway, broke out into the open internet, and autonomously compromised Hugging Face infrastructure in one of history's most unprecedented AI safety incidents. The post When the Safety Test Became the Threat: The Machine That Found Its Own Way Out appeared first on MarkT

items.title: Sakana AI’s LLM Peer Review System Catches 73% of Core-Claim Errors
items.summary: Sakana AI’s TMLR paper introduces Multi-Layered Review, a 3-agent Claude-based reviewer, and a 1,164-error Contradiction Benchmark. MLR caught 73.43% of core-claim errors, versus 14.81% for the best prior system.

items.summary: Tomorrow and Tuesday. If you see this you’re in!

items.title: Satya Nadella says we should assume all AI models are ‘compromised’
items.summary: In a lengthy post on X, Microsoft's CEO laid out his views on the dangers posed by highly advanced AI models and how to confront those risks. Nadella says we can no longer accept a world where AI is treated as a "set of nested black boxes" whose advice and actions we simply accept or […]

items.title: OrcaRouter Releases OrcaCyber Zero 1.5 Cybersecurity Model With 1M Context
items.summary: OrcaRouter released OrcaCyber Zero 1.5, a gated cybersecurity model with a 1M-token context window. It reports 100% on Cybench and 95.8% on an evaluable CVE-Bench subset, priced at $3.00 / $7.50 per 1M tokens.

items.title: Odyssey-3 is a new generative world model that you can try for free
items.summary: Odyssey is making its world model Odyssey-3 available as a public research preview. The 14-billion-parameter model generates interactive environments from text prompts in real time and can reportedly control robots, drones, and even GTA V.

items.title: Microsoft's Nadella bows to Trump's language diktat on "Super Intelligence" and uses it to attack OpenAI and Anthropic
items.summary: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella now calls artificial intelligence "super intelligence" instead of artificial intelligence, falling in line with Trump's preferred language. In his latest blog post, he frames AI models as insider security threats, taking yet another shot at OpenAI and Anthropic.

items.title: ArXiv caps submissions at two per month as AI paper flood overwhelms the preprint server
items.summary: Starting October 2026, arXiv will cap submissions at two per person per month. Monthly submissions have doubled in two years, and in the cs.AI category they've grown more than sixfold.

items.title: Cheaper AI tokens are driving more demand, and that's Jensen Huang's best-case scenario
items.summary: Data from a16z shows a Jevons paradox in the AI market: token prices keep falling, but H100 GPU rental prices hold steady or climb. Cheaper AI drives demand faster than costs drop.

items.title: Learning to use local AI is exciting, overwhelming, and frustrating
items.summary: I'm embarking on a journey I've so far been hesitant to go on: actually using AI on the regular. Giving my most personal data to cloud services has been a major hold up for me, but it's increasingly possible to run powerful models locally to see what they're capable of.

items.title: I Made Terrible Games With Google’s AI Playground
items.summary: A long day’s haul in the video game slop mines.

items.title: Agentic Systems: A Practitioner's Guide to 6 Advanced Architectural Patterns
items.summary: Beyond basic ReAct loops: six production-oriented architectures for building autonomous, reliable, and scalable LLM agents. The post Agentic Systems: A Practitioner's Guide to 6 Advanced Architectural Patterns appeared first on Towards Data Science .

items.title: AI agents overstate their results and remain far from autonomous research, study finds
items.summary: Epoch AI and Anthropic independently found the same thing: current AI models like GPT-5.6 Sol and Claude Fable 5 can run experiments but lack scientific self-criticism and genuine creative thinking. At best, Sol reached 15 percent of the human reference score, and even that came from methods researchers already knew.

items.title: A Practical Guide to OpenAI's New Decisions API
items.summary: Is this the JEV killer? The post A Practical Guide to OpenAI's New Decisions API appeared first on Towards Data Science .

items.title: AI agent teams waste massive tokens for barely measurable quality gains, research finds
items.summary: Teams of AI agents barely outperform solo agents but cost up to 5.1x more, according to Vals AI. Only one out of four tests with GPT-6 Sol and Claude Opus 5.5 showed a measurable gain.

items.title: Silicon Valley is falling in line with Trump’s attempt to rename AI
items.summary: When President Donald Trump announced his plans to rebrand artificial intelligence as "super intelligence," you'd be forgiven for being skeptical that it would catch on. While most of the broader population is sticking with AI, some of Silicon Valley's most powerful are falling in line and trying to give Trump the great AI rebrand he […]

items.title: What is Decision 3.0? vLLM Semantic Router’s New Open Decision Models
items.summary: vLLM Semantic Router released Decision 3.0, 5 Apache-2.0 multimodal decision models from 0.8B to 27B. They answer choice, yes/no and score questions about text and images in one call, without generating text.

items.title: Meet Cloudflare Clef-omni: A 30B-A3B Multimodal Decision Model for Audio, Video, Image and Text
items.summary: Cloudflare released Clef-omni, an Apache-2.0 multimodal decision model built on Qwen3-Omni-30B-A3B. It scores text, images, audio and video in one call for $0.15 per million input tokens, while Clef-flash drops to $0.038.

items.title: TII Releases Falcon-ASR: 1.6B Arabic Speech Model Hits 20.92% WER
items.summary: TII has released Falcon-ASR, a 1.6B speech recognition model for Arabic with an Emirati focus. It reports 20.92% average WER on 6 Arabic test sets, but weights and an API are not yet available.

items.title: Top 12 AI Live Translation Tools in 2026: Latency, Languages, Pricing
items.summary: We checked 12 AI live translation tools, including Palabra.ai, Google Live Translate, DeepL Voice, Teams Interpreter and Wordly, against official pages for languages, latency, platforms and pricing. The post Top 12 AI Live Translation Tools in 2026: Latency, Languages, Pricing appeared first on MarkTechPost .

items.title: Google Deepmind's AlphaProof Nexus solved dozens of open math problems and actually got peer reviewed
items.summary: Google Deepmind's AlphaProof Nexus solved dozens of open math problems, including nine Erdős problems two of which were unsolved for 56 years, per a study in Science. The publication comes as OpenAI faces a boycott for dumping AI proofs on GitHub without peer review.

items.title: Learning to Play Like a Pro: Adaptive Motion Planning and Tracking for Humanoid Robots
items.summary: This White Paper provides roboticists and control engineers with a comprehensive overview of how motion planning and motion tracking can be decoupled to preserve professional athletic style in humanoid robots, and why adaptive, speed-aware control is essential for closing the gap between simulation and real-world deployment. What you will learn about: Why combining a professional athlete’s motion

items.title: I Built a Trap for AI Image Judges. They Walked Into a Different One.
items.summary: Three vision AI models ignored the pretty image, yet GPT-4o invented answers and Claude kept answering B. The post I Built a Trap for AI Image Judges.

items.title: We Specified an AI Agent in 2016. We Called It Analytics.
items.summary: Re-reading my own IBM patent on real-time concert feedback as what it actually was: an agentic loop with multimodal perception, memory-grounded inference, and a human in the loop. What it got right, and what a decade of hindsight teaches agent builders today.

items.title: Amazon has over 1 million robot workers. What’s next for human employees?
items.summary: The second-largest corporate employer has bet big on robot workers to scale.

items.title: Anthropic's Andrej Karpathy says "the external world has seen the preview" of what AI can actually do
items.summary: Andrej Karpathy, co-founder of OpenAI and now at Anthropic, sees a widening knowledge gap in AI. About 75 percent of the world's population has barely touched LLMs.

items.title: Microsoft’s new AI chip makes it less reliant on Nvidia’s GPUs
items.summary: Microsoft is announcing its third-generation Maia in-house AI chip today, designed to be the "primary AI inference system" for Microsoft's products and services. Maia 300 not only improves the cost and efficiency of running AI workloads in the cloud, it's also more capable of handling the latest reasoning models and agentic tasks.
